# Steve Jobs interview by Swiss TV about Pixar 1996

**Source**: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MPxKzXd2Z-I

**Transcribed**: 2025-12-26 12:04

---

**[Steve Jobs]**: It's very wonderful, very beautiful, somewhat boring.
**[Speaker 2]**: Exactly.
**[Steve Jobs]**: But I say that of all of Switzerland in general, that strikes. I love it there, but great place to visit.
I love parts about the Swiss as much as I know them, like a very strong feeling about quality.
You know, which I love. I mean, really they're perfectionists, they like quality.
But pretty conservative.
**[Speaker 2]**: Oh, very.
**[Steve Jobs]**: Pretty conservative.
**[Speaker 2]**: So Steve Jobs, you founded Pixar in 1986 when you bought that computer's uh uh division of Lucas Film. Did you know right then what was going to happen in this business? Did you already envision that this was going to be a major business 10 years after?
**[Steve Jobs]**: Um, well, when I first met Ed Catmull, who ran the computer division of Lucas Film and who I founded Pixar with, we did it together.
Um, Ed showed me what they were working on and I was, I was blown away. I mean the graphics were, you know, years beyond anything I'd ever seen before.
And he told me of his dream to make the first computer animated feature film. And uh, I bought into that dream both sort of emotionally and financially, and we founded Pixar. And so we that dream has been what's driving us, uh, that dream has driven us for the last 10 years. And we finally did it. Uh, it took longer than we thought it would, but most things in life do take longer than than I, I think they will.
Um, but we did believe that we could um, could achieve that milestone sooner or later. Yeah.
**[Speaker 2]**: You expected it was going to take that much time to achieve?
**[Steve Jobs]**: No, I thought we would do it faster, but uh, I'm always anxious, so.
**[Speaker 2]**: So actually, how do you see the technology? There are so many things being done out there, not just at Pixar, but uh, if we look at the web, if we look at different things, do you think all these different novelties are going to merge in one way or another with all these, what is the next big thing that you see out there?
**[Steve Jobs]**: Uh, well, clearly the internet's really big. But you know, mostly I'm focused on what we're doing here at Pixar, which is to, you know, create awesome technology that I think is years ahead, maybe 10 years ahead of what anyone else is doing. But in service of the storytelling. And uh, this is what I I stay mostly focused on. And we don't, you know, our competitors are not like Microsoft or another studio even. We're not competing against somebody else making a film. We're competing against can we make a great film? That's our competition.
